source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1958, p. 6 ("Londonderry (nominations)"); Derry Journal, 9 May 1958, p. 1 ("No municipal election in Derry"); Derry Journal, 7 November 1958, p. 11
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: names as printed in the News-Letter's ward list of nominations (which does not separate aldermen and councillors); the aldermen are identified from the Derry Journal (Harvey and Hegarty, 9 May 1958) and from a Corporation division list styling Orr, Glover and Hamilton as aldermen and Jamieson and Buchanan as councillors (Derry Journal, 7 Nov 1958, p. 11); party by ward from the News-Letter's count of twelve Unionists and eight Nationalists

note: Triennial election of Londonderry Corporation (all twenty members: five aldermen and fifteen councillors), due Wednesday 21 May 1958: no contest. Twelve Unionists and eight Nationalists (Anti-Partitionists in the Derry Journal) were nominated for the twenty seats and returned unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1958, p. 6; Derry Journal, 9 May 1958, p. 1). New members: T. H. Buchanan (North, in place of Councillor E. J. Oxford), Seamus Deeney, Cornelius Glackin and Charles McDaid jun. (South); Councillors John P. Harvey and James Hegarty became aldermen in place of Aldermen E. G. McAteer and M. Coyle, who did not seek renomination. Returned unopposed.
